evidence: Verified the complete settled artifact and searched capability, negotiation, version, old/older peers, incompatible fields, semantics and migration equivalents. Root Message deadline contract requires every new durable ACK-required ordinary send to start at canonical committed send time, including unavailable/unbound recipients. The explicit negotiation rule in Invitation contract covers mutations requiring the new representation; all subtree validation clauses cover new incompatible fields. Root Risks ties negotiation to additive fields. ht-0lo.2.1 owns invitation wire capability refusal, while ht-0lo.1.1 owns receipt projections with existing timestamps/durations and no ordinary-send capability contract or mixed-version validation. The transactionally recorded schema/semantics marker is specified for canonical manifest/physical migration, not as a negotiated peer capability. No equivalent global minimum-daemon-version requirement or accepted mixed-version receipt limitation appears. Thus the spec leaves wire-compatible ordinary sends without a specified way to ensure the changed deadline behavior on an older daemon, materially weakening its bounded confirmation promise. This is an internal protocol-contract omission, not a claim about an external library or API.
